lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

Proportional Modified EBITDA of equity-method investments increased at Aux Sable Liquid Products LP primarily due to the absence of Williams’ $31 million share of a loss contingency accrual related to its former ownership in 2023, as well as the terms of the new product marketing agreement, partially offset by the sale of Williams’ investment in Aux Sable Liquid Products LP in the third quarter of 2024.

On August 1, 2024, Williams completed the sale of its equity-method investments in Aux Sable Liquid Products Inc., Aux Sable Liquid Products LP, and Aux Sable Midstream LLC (collectively, “Aux Sable”) in Williams’ Northeast G&P segment for total consideration of $ 161 million.
Williams is investing capital in the Louisiana LNG and Driftwood Pipeline projects, as well as the development of its Wamsutter upstream oil and gas properties.

During 2025, investing and financing expenditures included $4.9 billion of capital expenditures, including the Rimrock, Saber, and Driftwood Pipeline asset purchases as well as Power Innovation projects; $2.4 billion of dividends paid to common shareholders; and $0.5 billion of investments in unconsolidated affiliates, including Cogentrix and Louisiana LNG.

Appalachia Midstream Investments: Williams’ equity-method investments with an approximate average 66 percent interest in multiple gas gathering systems in the Marcellus Shale region

In October 2025, Williams closed on various agreements with the same counterparty to acquire a 10 percent equity-method investment in Louisiana LNG LLC (Louisiana LNG), which is developing a fully permitted LNG export facility, and an 80 percent interest in Driftwood Pipeline LLC (Driftwood Pipeline), which is constructing a fully permitted greenfield pipeline, Line 200, connecting to multiple other pipelines, including Transco and Louisiana Energy Gateway, to supply the LNG facility.

Williams owns a 50 percent equity-method investment in Gulfstream Natural Gas System, L.L.C. (Gulfstream), a 745-mile interstate natural gas pipeline system extending from the Mobile Bay area in Alabama to markets in Florida, which has a capacity to transport 1.4 Bcf/d. Operating responsibilities for Gulfstream are shared with the other 50 percent owner.
Appalachia Midstream Investments

Through the Appalachia Midstream Investments, Williams operates and owns an approximate average 66 percent interest in the Bradford Supply Hub gathering system and operates and owns an approximate average 68 percent interest in the Marcellus South gathering system, together which consist of approximately 1,108 miles of gathering pipeline in the Marcellus Shale region with the capacity to gather 5,870 MMcf/d of natural gas.

Williams operates and owns a 69 percent interest in a joint venture, Laurel Mountain Midstream, LLC (Laurel Mountain), which includes a 1,151-mile gathering system in western Pennsylvania with the capacity to gather 0.9 Bcf/d of natural gas.
